differences.reason: vue-tsc loses the spelling hint here because TypeScript's checker stops offering suggestions once a program has produced maximumSuggestionCount = 10 unresolved-name errors (onFailedToResolveSymbol in checker.ts increments the counter on every failed name resolution, including the ones generated virtual code never surfaces). Corsa does not implement that cap, so vize keeps the hint. The symbol tables agree: renaming this SFC so it is checked first makes vue-tsc 3.3.4 emit the identical TS2552 on an otherwise byte-identical program, and vize's virtual TypeScript for this file is byte-identical whether the sibling SFCs are in the program or not. Matching vue-tsc would mean rewriting TS2552 to TS2304 from a program-global, file-order-dependent counter, which is unstable under incremental checking and would silently drop genuine hints after the tenth unresolved name in any project.

vize.message: Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite. (source: <CountTo v-bind="props" @started="onStarted" @finished="onFinished" />; binding: @started)

differences.reason: Spreading this reactive() object (v-bind="props") exceeds TypeScript instantiation depth; the same spread in a plain .ts file reports TS2589 under both TypeScript 6 and 7. vue-tsc emits the props call too, but the checker anchors the error on the unmapped call start, so vue-tsc drops it. Vize reports it on the component tag the props literal maps to, because dropping a give-up hides why the props and listeners of this usage are degraded.

Vue's inline renderer reads that binding (`ref_key: "name", ref: name`), so it is used: removing it changes which element the template ref receives. Vize counts that read (#11386), so the TS6133 the directive expects does not occur and TypeScript reports the directive itself. vue-tsc writes template refs only as a JSDoc navigation comment, so the binding looks unread there.

vize.message: Type '"visible"' is not assignable to type 'Booleanish | undefined'. (source: aria-expanded="visible")

differences.reason: `Input` declares no `aria-expanded` prop and renders a root `<input>`, so the attribute falls through to that element, where Vue types `aria-expanded` as `Booleanish`. `"visible"` is not a valid ARIA state value (only true or false). Vize checks fallthrough attributes against the root element, and vue-tsc reports the same TS2322 here with `vueCompilerOptions.fallthroughAttributes` enabled. By default vue-tsc accepts any undeclared component attribute through `Record<string, unknown>`.
